name: St Nicholas the Wonderworker
title: Archbishop of Myra in Lycia
summary: The kind bishop who secretly gave gold to the poor, calmed storms at sea, and rescued the innocent — loved by children everywhere.
sourceNote: The text for older readers follows the order and content of the Life of St Nicholas in St Dimitri of Rostov's Lives of the Saints (December 6), retold in our own English words. The versions for younger readers are simplified retellings. Draft — awaiting review.

gold.caption: At night Nicholas secretly drops a bag of gold through the poor man's window.
gold.alt: A moonlit town at night. Young Nicholas, in a dark cloak with a golden halo, tosses a bag of gold through the lit window of a small house while three sisters sleep inside and a cat watches from the roof.

storm.caption: On the stormy sea, Nicholas prays and the wind and waves grow calm.
storm.alt: A wooden ship with a red-striped sail tossed on huge waves under dark clouds and lightning. Nicholas stands on the deck praying, and golden light breaks through the clouds as frightened sailors hold the ropes.

three-men.caption: Nicholas grabs the executioner's sword and saves three innocent men.
three-men.alt: A town square below a fortress. Bishop Nicholas in red vestments holds back the sword of an executioner while three kneeling men look up in hope. Soldiers, townspeople and three Roman generals watch.
